text:
simon: Quick follow-up on progressive rollout for model variants. I've sketched a small policy engine that lives in the router and decides: A/B split for feature experiments, weighted canaries, and automatic downgrade to a smaller/quantized model when SLOs break. Need tradeoffs and interface boundaries before I spin up a prototype.

anya: +1. We should separate concerns: policy evaluation (decisions) vs execution (routing). Keep the runtime shim tiny.

raj: Important Q: what signals do we use to trigger fallback? latency-only is easy but risky for quality.

michaela: My vote is multi-signal: latency (p95), error-rate (5xxs + inference failures), and quality drift measured on a rolling sample. Fallback if latency>target OR error_rate spikes OR quality delta > threshold.

simon: Agree. Also need to decide who owns the sampled-quality check — runtime collects samples, evaluation runs in control-plane periodically. That keeps runtime fast.

raj: How do we avoid cascading fallbacks during ramp? If lots of canaries fall back to smaller model, we might overload the smaller pool.

anya: Capacity-aware policies: policy eval should be able to query capacity snapshot (available qps/capacity) and rate-limit fallbacks. e.g. only allow X% of traffic to downgrade per region in a rolling window.

michaela: Also require a soft cooldown per candidate model and a global circuit-breaker. Pseudocode YAML for the policy proto:```yaml
policy_version: v1
matchers:
  - name: experiment_alpha
    traffic_split: 10  # percent
    monitors:
      - name: latency_p95
        window: 1m
        threshold_ms: 220
      - name: error_rate
        window: 1m
        threshold_percent: 1.0
    actions:
      - on_violation: downgrade_to: model-small-quantized
        cooldown: 5m
global_limits:
  max_downgrade_percent: 20
  capacity_check: true
```

raj: That looks good. A couple of interface concerns:
- runtime needs a lightweight policy eval client, not full proto parsing per request.
- decision cache for N seconds to avoid hot loops.

anya: For the runtime shim implement an async refresh of the decision table and a synchronous lookup by key (model_id, region, route). Keep the decision format flat, e.g.: `{action: "serve", variant: "model-a", weight: 90}` per route.

simon: Operational integrations: we must emit an event when a decision changes for a route (so console can show canary state) and when an automatic downgrade happens (for SRE + alerts).

michaela: Also add a debug header for requests routed via fallback so we can trace regressions: `x-rw-fallback: model-small-quantized;policy=latency_p95`.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary run started: canary-2026-04-05T15:12Z for model-experiment-alpha (10% traffic).

raj: Action items: I will prototype a router client that consumes a compact decision blob. ETA EOW.

anya: I'll add metrics plumbing to Console (canary state + downgrade counts) and a UI widget to toggle verbose debug headers.

michaela: I'll draft a short RFC on the policy proto (edge cases, cooldown semantics, capacity gating).

simon: Cool. One design tradeoff note: we are intentionally avoiding per-request offline evaluation (costly) — we'll rely on sampling for quality. If we decide online quality scoring later, we should scope it as an opt-in extension.

raj: +1. Also we should add a canary rolloff plan: automatic rollback vs gradual traffic decrease. Prefer gradual rollback with metric-based checkpoints.

anya: Can we also annotate models with an "upgrade_tier" (e.g., hot/cold) so router can prefer hot variants when routing heavy tail?

michaela: Nice idea. Put that in the proto as metadata.

simon: OK — consensus seems to be: small policy proto, runtime decision cache, sampled quality checks in control plane, capacity-aware global limits, and observability hooks. I'll start a prototype and ping you all for feedback. :rocket:

anya: Thanks — ping when you have the proto, will wire Console. :thumbsup:
